title: Interquartile Burn Allocator & Price-Deferral Protocol — working sheet
content:
Summary:
This working sheet defines an operational rule-set (the "Interquartile Burn Allocator") to partition available runway into conservative spending bands, plus a complementary "Price-Deferral Protocol" that specifies conditional pricing and hiring actions when burn moves between bands. Purpose is to (1) extend runway predictably, (2) preserve high-priority hires, (3) tune price nudges to reduce token demand without sudden enterprise disruption.

Objectives:
- Create an automated, auditable set of triggers that translate burn/usage signals into pricing or hiring levers.
- Prioritize headcount retention for product and SRE for minimal service degradation.
- Bias actions to temporary deferrals and non-headcount levers first (GPU spot rebalancing, quantization rollout).

Key assumptions (base case):
- Cash on hand: $85,000,000
- Monthly net cash burn (current): $6,900,000
- Committed Dedicated GPU spend: $1,800,000/mo (30% of infra cost)
- Spot/variable inference cost: $1,200,000/mo
- Average effective token price to customers (current): $0.0009 per token
- Hiring pipeline (open reqs): 22 FTEs (across Eng/Product/Finance/CS)

Input snapshot (base numbers):
line,item,amount
1,starting_cash,85000000
2,monthly_burn_current,6900000
3,committed_gpu_monthly,1800000
4,variable_infra_monthly,1200000
5,open_headcount_reqs,22
6,avg_token_price_current,0.0009

Interquartile Burn Allocator (logic):
- Compute effective monthly burn distribution over last 6 months; take IQR (Q1, Q2, Q3). Define three bands: Green (below Q1), Amber (Q1-Q3), Red (above Q3).
- Map runway months to bands using: runway = cash / burn. For operational simplicity we round to nearest 0.25 months.
- Allocation rule: when in Amber, activate non-HC levers; when crossing Red, initiate staged headcount deferral per matrix below; when returning to Green, reverse deferrals in priority order.

Example calculation (simulated):
- Historical monthly burns used: [6.2M, 6.7M, 6.9M, 7.1M, 6.5M, 6.8M] -> Q1=6.5M, Q3=6.95M -> Green <6.5M, Amber 6.5-6.95M, Red >6.95M.
- With current burn 6.9M -> Amber band. Current runway = 85M / 6.9M = 12.3 months -> nominally safe but Amber triggers non-HC actions to preserve cushion.

Price-Deferral Protocol (steps):
1) Soft price nudge: +6% effective token price (elasticity estimate -0.18) implemented as rolling throttle for new low-value trial accounts (2-week scope). Measure response in 7d.
2) Routing & model-tilt: shift 8% of non-latency-sensitive traffic to lower-cost quantized variant (targeted by route tags).
3) Committed/spot reallocation: up to 20% additional spot ordering for non-SLA burst capacity during Amber.
4) If burn crosses Red for two consecutive weeks -> apply HC Stage-1 (freeze non-essential reqs, pause external contractor renewals).
5) If burn remains in Red for four weeks -> HC Stage-2 (defer 8–16% of open reqs per matrix; negotiate 30-day delayed starts for new offers).

Headcount phasing matrix (open reqs = 22):
role,open_reqs,priority,stage1_deferral_pct,stage2_deferral_pct
1,backend-eng,7,low,10,25
2,infra-sre,4,high,0,5
3,product-design,3,medium,25,40
4,ml-inference,5,high,5,15
5,go-to-market,3,low,30,50

Intervention sensitivity scenarios (simple):
Scenario A (soft): price +6% + routing tilt 8% -> projected burn reduction = 4.5% -> new burn = 6.59M -> runway = 12.9 months.
Scenario B (moderate): price +12% + 15% model tilt + 10% headcount defer (stage2 partial) -> projected burn reduction = 11.8% -> new burn = 6.07M -> runway = 14.0 months.
Scenario C (severe): price +20% + 25% model tilt + 30% headcount defer -> projected burn reduction = 23.4% -> new burn = 5.28M -> runway = 16.1 months.

Trade-offs noted:
- Price nudges above ~15% risk churn in high-MRR enterprise cohorts; require account-level credits/SLAs to mitigate.
- Model-tilt reduces unit cost but increases backend complexity and introduces small latency regressions for some routes; track per-route error budget.
- HC deferral concentrated in GTM and low-priority backend roles preserves SRE and core inference hires.

Operational playbook (quick runbook):
- Weekly: compute 6-month rolling burn IQR on Tuesday morning; if band changes, finance informs PM/sre/ops owners with recommended actions.
- Day 0 Amber: enable Step 1 & 2 (price nudge + model-tilt) for 2 weeks, instrument 7/30 day impact windows.
- If Amber persists past 21 days -> escalate to Stage-1 HC pause (legal/people notified).
- If Red persists -> Stage-2 executed with 14-day notice windows on offers; CFO signoff required for any new offers during active Stage-2.

Open questions / items for next iteration:
- Elasticity calibrations by customer cohort (enterprise vs self-serve) need product telemetry feed (Confluence-9876 placeholder).
- Define per-route latency SLO impact limits for model-tilt (input from SRE/infra).
- Contract language for delayed offer starts (people ops / legal check).

Quick action items (this doc):
- Miguel: wire up weekly IQR report to Finance dashboard (JIRA-FIN-1245).
- Priya: draft comms for enterprise credit guardrails for price nudges.
- Ethan: run a 2-week quantized-tilt A/B on non-enterprise routes and capture latency/regression deltas.

Notes: this is intentionally conservative and operational-first. The sheet is a living instrument — prefer iteration over a single heavy-handed pricing move. Keep human-in-loop for Stage-2 HC decisions.
